result:
Compilation succeeded. I've added two self-contained JUnit 3.8 (`junit.framework.TestCase`) test classes under `tests/com/google/gson/stream/`:

- **`JsonReaderAgentTest`** — covers construction, `beginArray/endArray/beginObject/endObject/hasNext/peek`, name/string/boolean/null/int/long/double readers (including numeric-as-string and string-as-number coercion per the doc), `skipValue`, `isLenient/setLenient` and the specific lenient relaxations called out in the javadoc (non-execute prefix, multiple top-level values, top-level scalars), documented error cases (`NumberFormatException` on overflow/non-exact/non-finite conversions, `IllegalStateException` on wrong-type reads and after `close()`, `IOException` on structural mismatches), plus `getPath()` and `toString()`.
- **`JsonWriterAgentTest`** — covers empty/nested array and object writing (mirrored from the class javadoc's own example to avoid guessing output format), string escaping, all `value(...)` overloads, `nullValue`/`jsonValue`, `serializeNulls` semantics (including the "no effect on array elements" rule), fluent `this`-returning methods, `lenient` top-level/non-finite-number relaxations, `htmlSafe` escaping, `flush`/`close` delegation to the underlying `Writer`, `close()` failing on an incomplete document, and `IllegalStateException` for malformed-JSON calls per the class-level contract.

Every expectation traces back to the javadoc contract in `api/`; where the contract was silent on exact exception types (e.g. `name(null)`), I asserted the weakest documented guarantee (a `RuntimeException`) rather than guessing an implementation detail. `./compile.sh` reports `compiled OK`.
